metric_definitions.agreed_by_all: every declared participant names the same winner, counted from each participant's own recorded vector
metric_definitions.app_messages_ingested: ONE inbound application-level message a participant examined at receive time. baseline: every payload the collector loop read (appended unconditionally, as at :506). exp13: the sum of the real inbox lengths passed to run_round(). Neither value is derived from an arithmetic formula about what the arm would have exchanged.
metric_definitions.app_messages_sent: ONE application-level protocol message produced by a participant and handed to its transport inside the episode. baseline: 1 request + 1 ACCEPT per answering candidate, counted at the send. exp13: 1 belief per non-censored round per active agent, read from each negotiator's own beliefs_published counter. Transport duplicates re-offered at receive time add receipts, never sends.
metric_definitions.convergence_time_s: slowest converged participant's monotonic interval from first belief to confirmed agreement, inside this one process; None when agreement never happened. NOT a robot or network latency.
metric_definitions.dds_or_network_packets: NOT MEASURED — no transport exists in this process
metric_definitions.decided: derived from the arm's end state: baseline owner COMMITTED with a winner; exp13 every declared participant terminal AND converged
metric_definitions.expected_winner: per-arm rule, NOT a shared oracle. baseline: 'highest utility among those heard, ties keep arrival order' — which is the model's own rule, so winner_matched_expected is tautological for the baseline and is not evidence about it. exp13: 'highest utility, ties by lowest agent id', an independent statement of the module's documented rule, so its match rate is evidence
metric_definitions.milliseconds: reported only as measured single-process intervals with the tick disclosed; no millisecond figure here is a protocol latency
metric_definitions.outcome_class: one rule for both arms: CONVERGED / UNDECIDED / STALLED_NOT_TERMINAL / FAILED, from observed end state
metric_definitions.rounds: arm-specific: baseline 1 is definitional (single window); exp13 is the highest observed per-participant round counter. Never converted between arms.
metric_definitions.selection_list_size: per-arm and NOT comparable: baseline = receipts the sort keyed on; exp13 = participants whose own state reported converged. It is never used as a message count
metric_definitions.sequential_activation_probe: distinct Exp-13 winners over every one-at-a-time activation order with identical utilities. Added because the lockstep determinism probe cannot see an activation-order defect at all

naming_change: this revision renamed frames_sent -> app_messages_sent and ingestion_attempts -> app_messages_ingested, and replaced the previous exp13 ingestion formula rounds x (N-1) with counted inboxes
non_equivalences_disclosed: one-sided baseline vs symmetric Exp-13: only the baseline's owner holds a decision
stopping rules differ by construction (fixed window vs all-agreement / round bound / deadline) and are not convertible
the baseline excludes the owner from its candidate pool; Exp-13 lets it bid and retain
candidate refusal counts are definitional for the baseline, not observed, because the modelled collector has no admission test
